title: 2022年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2022年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 In the age of the internet, there's no such thing as a private debate. But is that bad for science? Some scientists have had concerns. When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public. Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices. If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems—and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly—then this is good for everyone, including scientists.

P2 A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced. Issues such as safety of the product and perception of the public were examined and considered. But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine.

P3 The anxiety seems misplaced. Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place.

P4 For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules. But rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self- correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. With the validity of science coming under attack, there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life. Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all.

questions.q: What does the author think open debate can do?
options: Help the public to better understand science.
Clear up confusion in the scientific community.
Settle disputes between universities and government agencies.
Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think open debate can do是一个具体的做什么问题，不含infer、 imply、mainly about等推断或主旨信号词，属于围绕一个话题点的细节定位题

【拆句】主干是What does the author think open debate can do，think后省略that，引出宾语 从句open debate can do (what)。问句的What其实是宾语从句里do的宾语，被前置到句 首。结构简单、无陷阱。 51. What does the author think open debate can do? A) Help the public to better understand science. B) Clear up confusion in the scientific community. C) Settle disputes between universities and government agencies. D) Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public.

【定位】If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems— and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly —then this is good for everyone, including scientists. 如果这一趋势能推动科学家更快地就我们面临问题的最佳解决方案达成一致，并同时帮助公 众更清楚地观察科学讨论的过程，那么对所有人，包括科学家在内，都是好事。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly ↔ Help the public to better understand science 预判让公众更清楚地观察、理解科学讨论与Help the public to better understand science在语义上同构，仅是observe到understand、scientific discourse到science的 上下位替换 B) 偷换概念 Clear up confusion in the scientific community说的是消除科学界内部的困惑，但原 文potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion点 明confusion存在于公众一侧、而非科学界内部 C) 无中生有 Settle disputes between universities and government agencies声称开放辩论能解 决高校与政府机构之间的纠纷；原文虽提及halls of universities and government agencies，但只是说辩论的发生地，并未说要去settle什么disputes D) 与原文相反 Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public把防止信息被误用说 成open debate的功能；但原文there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion里，这一可能性是开放辩论的副作用而非它的 解决目标 为什么《纽约时报》上发表的一场近期辩论在专家中引起了担忧? A) 它可能会阻碍医学研究的进展。 B) 它可能会滋生公众对现代医学的不信任。 C) 它可能会增加获取研究资金的难度。 D) 它可能会妨碍医学科学家达成共识。

questions.q: Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts?
options: It might hinder the progress in medical research.
It might breed public distrust in modern medicine.
It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds.
It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts问的是某一具体事件下专家担心的具体原因，原因可在文中直接找到，不需要跨段 推断 52. Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts? A) It might hinder the progress in medical research. B) It might breed public distrust in modern medicine. C) It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds. D) It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus.

【拆句】主干是Why加did加a recent debate加arouse加concerns。a recent debate后带过去分词 短语published in The New York Times作后置定语，限定是哪一场debate；among experts限定concerns的范围。理清后题干即那场登在某报上的辩论，为何让专家担心。

【定位】But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine. 但一些专家担心，这种公开揣测可能让人们相信：对细节的分歧意味着科学界对现代医药的 安全与效率缺乏足够的共识。

【选项】A) 无中生有 It might hinder the progress in medical research谈的是阻碍医学研究的进展，原文 只说公开辩论可能让公众产生误解，并未说会拖慢医学研究本身 B) ✓ 正确 might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine ↔It might breed public distrust in modern medicine 预判中的对现代医药产生不信任正好对应public distrust in modern medicine；原文的 多步表述被压缩成一个名词distrust，是典型的名词化同义替换 C) 无中生有 It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds说会增加获得研究经费的难 度；原文从未提及funds、funding、money相关概念 D) 偷换概念 It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus说会阻止医学科学家达成共 识；原文是meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus——即让公众以为科学界 没共识，但事实是科学界已有共识，并不是公开辩论会真的让科学家无法达成共识 为什么作者说一些专家的焦虑似乎是错位的? A) 在会议上辩论科学问题现在已经过时了。 B) 科学家和公众都可以辩论各种话题。 C) 无论如何公众都能接触到关于科学的辩论。 D) 科学家可以用任何他们喜欢的方式表达自己的观点。

questions.q: Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced?
options: Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned.
Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public.
Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway.
Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced问的是作者下此判断 的依据，依据明示在原文紧随其后的句子中，属于因果细节 53. Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced? A) Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned. B) Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public. C) Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway. D) Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like.

【拆句】Why does the author say后接一个宾语从句some experts' anxiety seems misplaced。 anxiety前是some experts'所有格作定语；seems是系动词、misplaced是表语形容词。理 解为为什么作者说某些专家的担心是放错地方的。

【定位】Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place. 去开会、在会上辩论科学问题的日子已经过去了，这是好事，因为那些聚会不够多元，把许 多重要的声音排除在外。如今，无论辩论在哪里举行，公众都能接触到。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned只是原文Gone are the days of going to a conference的复述，确实存在于文中，但它只是支撑句之一， 不是作者用来回答为什么misplaced的核心理由；核心理由是公众如今随处可获取辩论 B) 偷换概念 Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public说的是多元话题可 被科学家与公众共同辩论；原文diverse是修饰those gatherings本身（聚会不够多 元），并不是说话题多元，更没说公众能与科学家共同辩论 C) ✓ 正确 the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place ↔ Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway 预判中的无论在哪都能接触到正是accessible to the public anyway的内涵；从access （动词）到accessible（形容词）的词性转换加主被动互换是四级最典型的同义替换手法 D) 张冠李戴 Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like说的是科学家可以以他们 喜欢的方式发声；原文谈论的是公众能接触到辩论，主语和动作都不是科学家 作者建议科学家如何对待公开辩论? A) 对此进行更多讨论。 B) 张开双臂拥抱它。 C) 为它制定新规则。 D) 将它限制在理性的程度。

questions.q: What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate?
options: Have more discussions about it.
Embrace it with open arms.
Formulate new rules for it.
Restrain it to a rational degree.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate问的是一个具体建 议，答案在原文祈使句中能直接找到，无需推断 54. What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate? A) Have more discussions about it. B) Embrace it with open arms. C) Formulate new rules for it. D) Restrain it to a rational degree.

【拆句】主干What does the author suggest scientists do。suggest后接的是宾语从句省略 that，scientists是从句主语、do是从句动词（虚拟语气省略should），about public debate是范围状语。句意：作者建议科学家们对于公共辩论应该怎么做。

【定位】But rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. 但与其回避这类对话，不如让辩论变得透明而有力，无论它们在哪里举行。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Have more discussions about it说对公共辩论本身展开更多讨论——它把公共辩论变 成被讨论的对象；原文是要科学家参与到公共辩论中，而不是开会讨论公共辩论应不应 该做 B) ✓ 正确 rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous ↔ Embrace it with open arms 预判拥抱并积极参与与Embrace it with open arms在意象与态度极性上完全一致； rather than avoiding的反面正是embrace C) 与原文相反 Formulate new rules for it说要为公共辩论制定新规则；原文it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules承认公共辩论缺规则，但下一句紧接着以But rather than avoiding such conversations转向拥抱而非立规则，作者并未建议立新规 D) 与原文相反 Restrain it to a rational degree说要把公共辩论约束到一个合理程度；原文却用let the debates be transparent and vigorous强调放开而非约束，方向相反 作者在最后一段关于科学说了什么? A) 它是通过教科书传播的。 B) 它是被证明有效且符合实际的东西。 C) 它是一个动态的自我完善过程。 D) 它是事实和既定规则的集合。

questions.q: What does the author say about science in the last paragraph?
options: It is transmitted through textbooks.
It is what proves valid and true to life.
It is a dynamic and self-improving process.
It is a collection of facts and established rules.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about science in the last paragraph问的是末段里关于 science的具体描述，不问全文主旨也不问态度极性，定位段已给出，属段内细节题

【拆句】主干What does the author say about science。in the last paragraph是地点状语限定回 答范围。say about science是动词搭配对…作出说明。理解为在末段里作者关于science说 了什么。 55. What does the author say about science in the last paragraph? A) It is transmitted through textbooks. B) It is what proves valid and true to life. C) It is a dynamic and self-improving process. D) It is a collection of facts and established rules.

【定位】If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. 如果想让公众明白科学是一个光荣的自我修正过程，那么科学就是教科书里一组固定事实这 一观念就必须被抛弃。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It is transmitted through textbooks说科学通过教科书传播；原文the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed恰好是作者要否 定的观念 B) 张冠李戴 It is what proves valid and true to life说科学是被证明有效且符合现实的东西；原文 there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life里 true to life修饰的是scientific debates（辩论）如何被感知，而不是用来定义science 本身 C) ✓ 正确 science is an honorably self-correcting process ↔It is a dynamic and self-improving process 预判自我修正的动态过程与a dynamic and self-improving process逐字对应；self- correcting对应self-improving是同根同义的复合形容词替换 D) 与原文相反 It is a collection of facts and established rules说科学是事实与既定规则的集合—— 这与原文science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook想抛弃的旧观念完全对齐
